family.name: Content & Brand Marketing
family.summary: A B2B SaaS blog whose traffic doubled while trials stayed flat, a quarter's content bet, and a content brief that contradicts the customer research.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Traffic up, trials flat
stages.summary: Explain to the CEO why traffic doubled but trials did not. Think aloud: shows whether they judge content by intent, not volume.

stages.title: Next quarter's bet
stages.summary: Commit to how the next quarter's 12 pieces are spent and estimate the trial impact. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two months later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their bet. Tests whether they adapt and explain what happened.

stages.title: Review a freelancer's brief
stages.summary: Critique a content brief that contradicts the customer research and makes a false pricing claim. Think aloud.

stages.title: Positioning (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the comparison page positioning and headlines with any AI tool, and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI.

stages.title: A real piece of content
stages.summary: A real piece of content or campaign that didn't move the business metric. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You've just joined **Stackroom**, which sells inventory software for D2C brands. Its customers are operations leads at D2C brands. You lead content and brand; you have one writer and a freelance budget.

Blog traffic has grown from 26,950 to **49,000 sessions a month** in six months. Trials started from the blog went from 257 to **252** a month. About 17% of trials become paying customers at ₹2,999 a month.

brief.caption: Last month, by page
rows: How to set reorder points without a data team
Stackroom vs Stockwise: an honest comparison

items: Main reason they chose Stackroom: stock-out forecasts for every SKU (54%), integrations (17%), price (8%).
Stockwise is the competitor prospects mention most. It costs ₹2,249 a month.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Which brand do you think has the clearest voice right now, and how can you tell?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: The CEO says: **"Traffic doubled and trials didn't move. Is the blog a vanity project?"** What do you see in the numbers, and what do you tell them?
Refer to specific pages and figures. Stackroom's numbers are on the left.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Mostly in-depth how-to guides tied to the product
One flagship research report for brand and press
Refresh and re-optimise the existing top pages

prompt.text: You have capacity for **12 pieces** next quarter. Where does most of it go?
Pick one, then explain why, roughly how many extra trials a month you expect (and how you got that), and the risk you are accepting.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Mostly comparison and "alternative to" pages"

prompt.text: Comparison pages are bringing trials. But Stockwise's lawyer has emailed about a pricing claim on your comparison page, and Sales says these leads close at 12% versus 21% for other leads.
**What do you do this week, and what do you tell Sales?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Mostly in-depth how-to guides tied to the product"

prompt.text: After eight weeks only 3 of your new guides rank on page one, and blog trials are up just 8%. The CEO asks whether to stop.
**What do you tell the CEO, and what do you change?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "One flagship research report for brand and press"

prompt.text: The report was covered by two trade publications and earned 58 backlinks, but only 9 trials. The CEO asks if it was worth a quarter.
**What do you say, and what happens next quarter?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Refresh and re-optimise the existing top pages"

prompt.text: After cutting the fluff from top pages, blog traffic is down 28% but trials are up 27%. The board deck shows a falling traffic line and the CEO is nervous.
**How do you handle the board deck and the CEO?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A freelancer drafted the brief below for the "Stackroom vs Stockwise" page. **Name the three most important problems, most important first, and what you would change.**
You do not need to comment on every line.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: **Audience:** freelancers and students looking for free tools.
**Angle:** position Stackroom as the cheapest option on the market.
**Key message:** our sleek design and dark mode.
**Format:** include a side-by-side comparison table near the top.
**Call to action:** end with a newsletter sign-up box.
**Length:** about 1,500 words.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write a two-sentence positioning statement and three headline options for the "Stackroom vs Stockwise" page.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a piece of content or a campaign you were proud of that did not move the business metric.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
